items.text: On 2026-11-04 `parse()` in `src/index.ts` was fixed to tolerate leading/trailing whitespace by applying `str.trim()` before the regex match (`' 2d'` gives 172800000, `'1.5h '` gives 5400000). The length check still applies to the untrimmed string, and whitespace-only input like `'   '` still returns `NaN`. Motivation: YAML configs often yield padded values that previously returned NaN. Tests were added in `src/parse.test.ts` (including a whitespace-only case) with all 174 tests passing. Committed as `07a8d6b` "fix: tolerate leading and trailing whitespace in parse()" on `feat/compound-format`, not pushed; co-authored with Claude.

items.text: Compound mode for the short formatter was decided on 2026-11-04: `format(5400000, { compound: true })` returns `1h 30m` instead of `2h`. Original rules: largest unit first, zero parts skipped, parts separated by a space, smallest unit seconds (leftover milliseconds dropped), largest unit days (no weeks/months/years, so 400 days gives `400d`), negative values get a leading `-`. Unspecified edge cases chosen by the agent: values under one second (e.g. `500`) give `0s` rather than an empty string; negative sub-second values (`-500`) give `0s`, not `-0s`; when `long` and `compound` are both set, `long` wins (gives `2 hours`) and no long-form compound exists. The original version was implemented with tests (including long+compound; 173 tests passing) and a README section, and committed on `feat/compound-format` as `5c7b8bb` "feat: add compound option to short formatter" (not pushed, no PR). REVISED later on 2026-11-04: output must be Go `time.ParseDuration`-compatible because deploy logs are scraped by a Go service that runs every duration through `time.ParseDuration` (rejects spaces, has no `d` unit). Parts are glued together without spaces with hours as the biggest unit, e.g. `25h30m` instead of the earlier `1d 1h 30m`. This supersedes the space-separated, days-as-largest-unit format; the change is NOT yet implemented and is the next task (the committed implementation still uses the old format).

items.text: Early history of ms (2012): the project began with 'Initial import as repository' and a mocha fix. In early September 2012 TJ Holowaychuk built core functionality incrementally (string support, seconds/minutes/hours/days, ms(number) test refactor, component.json, more input flexibility). Releases 0.2.0 (2012-09-03) and 0.3.0 (2012-09-07) followed, with a fix for ms("100") breakage. Between September and November 2012 it gained component packaging (component.json version and license, broken client-side tests removed), rounding to fix long decimals, and a short formatting default with a `.long` option. Releases 0.4.0 (2012-10-22) and 0.5.0 (2012-11-09) shipped, and a license was added closing #18.
